content.title: How UCLA dominated South Carolina to win women’s NCAA Tournament championship
content.text: The Bruins captured their first NCAA title with a 79-51 win over the GamecocksUCLA celebrates its first-ever NCAA Tournament national title. Getty ImagesSKIP ADVERTISEMENTAdvertisementGabriela Jaquez on brother Jaime: 'Of course I have bragging rights'Gabriela Jaquez on older brother Jaime Jaquez Jr.:💬 “Of course, I have bragging rights, I’m a champion now. The impact he had on me is just really inspiring.” Getty ImagesCori Close is the first coach to win her first championship since 2017, when Dawn Staley led South Carolina to its first title.Betts explains throat issuesLauren Betts says she's (obviously) fine now re: her throat. 💬 "It's dry out here."Betts on sister, Sienna: 'She understands the moment'Lauren Betts on her championship performance: 💬 “At the end of the day, no one’s going to really care about how much you averaged this season when you have a freaking ring around your finger. No one cares.”On freshman Sienna Betts’ performance in the national championship: 💬 “She understands the moment.”Join our live reaction showEager to hear more analysis and insights from the women’s national championship game?Join “No Offseason,” The Athletic’s women’s basketball podcast, for a live reaction from Phoenix.The “No Offseason” cohosts Zena Keita and Layshia Clarendon will react to UCLA’s dominant victory over South Carolina.SKIP ADVERTISEMENTAdvertisementDawn Staley speaks on Cori Close Getty ImagesSouth Carolina coach Dawn Staley spoke about he relationship with UCLA coach Cori Close and how happy she is for her winning a national title. 💬 “Cori is one of those people who really works at making our game better. Not just UCLA, but our entire game. Although we didn’t win, I can swallow it because we lost to a really good human being and a good team that represents women’s basketball well.“The game finally paid her back.”UCLA's leaders explain team's confidenceUCLA’s veterans are on the dais talking about the team’s confidence.Kiki Rice: 💬 “Today was just a fantastic display of our resilience, intensity that we came out. Just our will to win. We knew, we had a feeling this was our time, this was our year. We came out there this entire weekend and we would not be denied.”Lauren Betts: 💬 “The confidence we came out with, we just knew we were going to win because of all the prep and work that we put in. I think when we find a way to play together and play selflessly, do what we do, no one can stop us.”Gabriela Jaquez: 💬 “Our mentality coming out, we all decided, I think that’s what made us this so powerful this whole season. When we decided we wanted to do something, we did it.”Cori Close and Kiki Rice rocking the champagne goggles at the dais.Let's hear from Dawn StaleyDawn Staley opened her news conference by giving her props to UCLA: 💬 “I thought they came out and disrupted from a defensive standpoint. Then they pretty much got what they wanted offensively. We just didn’t have it today. We tried, but we just didn’t have it today. They were the better team today. Congratulations to them.”Rice shares when UCLA knew it had a special groupKiki Rice talking seriously while staring into reporters’ eyes with champagne goggles on is hilarious.💬 "Right from the beginning, right when we all got on campus, we knew that this group was going to be special. You could just feel the energy.”SKIP ADVERTISEMENTAdvertisementRaven Johnson: 'I'm not satisfied with the outcome today' Getty ImagesRaven Johnson on the smile on her face after losing in the national championship game:💬 “I’m just a bubbly person. I’m not smiling. I’m actually mad. I’m actually mad. But my personality is making me smile through the pain, if that makes sense. I’m not satisfied with the outcome that happened today. I’m just smiling through the pain.”Betts' path to Most Outstanding Player Getty ImagesUCLA's Lauren Betts won Most Outstanding Player for her role in UCLA's first NCAA championship and her masterful performances along the way.Here is how Betts fared in each of the Bruins' six wins:First round against California Baptist: 22 points, 9-15 FG, 10 rebounds, 1 blockSecond round against Oklahoma State: 35 points, 15-19 FG, 9 rebounds, 1 blockSweet 16 against Minnesota: 16 points, 7-9 FG, 5 rebounds, 5 blocksElite Eight against Duke: 23 points, 9-14 FG, 10 rebounds, 5 blocksFinal Four against Texas: 16 points, 7-10 FG, 11 rebounds, 3 blocksNational Championship against South Carolina: 14 points, 6-10 FG, 11 rebounds, 2 blocksWhat a way to end her senior season!Cori Close’s opening statement: 💬 “It’s hard to even know what to say. ... I remember my dad used to say, he knew I loved to compete. He goes, ‘If you can take something that you love and continue to compete and impact people’s hearts in the process, you found a good thing.’ This has been a calling, not a job. I’ve been saying it all day, but I don’t even know how else to say it, it’s immeasurably more than I could ask or imagine.”Tessa Johnson: 'We don't like this feeling' Getty ImagesSouth Carolina’s Tessa Johnson spoke about the emotions of losing a championship game and what went wrong this afternoon.💬 “The look on our faces, we don't like this feeling. The standard is to get here, I expect our team to get here next year. We were prepared, but they out-rebounded us, by how many? A whole bunch. “We knew they could rebound but we still didn't box out and make the extra plays.”Raven Johnson: 'Score speaks for itself' Getty ImagesSouth Carolina’s Raven Johnson spoke on the difficulty scoring today: 💬 “See the score? Score speaks for itself."And the impact of Dawn Staley on her💬 "She means a lot to me. We’ve been through a lot together. It hurts that it couldn’t end the way we wanted it to end. She always be like a mother figure to me. I always come to her about every little thing. I love her.”SKIP ADVERTISEMENTAdvertisementA memorable moment for Betts familyOne more thought here, it's really cool that Lauren Betts' final game gets to be a championship win with her sister. That will surely be something her family never forgets.More from Lauren Betts Getty ImagesLauren Betts, wiping away tears on the stage, spoke about the platform she has beyond basketball and inspiring others.💬 “Basketball has given me the platform to change people’s lives. I told her (my mom) that I was put on this earth not to score points but to help people.” South Carolina's nine third-quarter points are the fewest third-quarter points in the championship game.Gabriela Jaquez: 'We decided to be national champions' The trophy presentation couldn’t end without hearing from Gabriela Jaquez, who had a memorable performance today in the women’s national championship game: “Just doing what I do, coming in, doing whatever the team needs and just really focusing on defense and rebounding this game. “I’m so proud of this group — we’re national champions and it feels amazing.“We decided to be national champions.”
